The Justice Department is drawing up contingency plans to potentially
intervene in next week's midterm elections, three officials with knowledge of
the discussions tell me.

The plans cover various "doomsday" scenarios seen as improbable but not
impossible. The Trump administration has hinted at them publicly in recent
weeks. National security officials tell me the hints reflect active
discussions about what to do if the outcome is disputed over things like
foreign interference, claims that noncitizens voted, or chaos at the polls.
